note: Why an artifact is not in the set, when the reason is a standing fact about this machine rather than something that happened during one run. capture.sh writes a per-run reason for anything that failed in that run, and that always wins; this is the fallback, so a run that did not attempt a scene still says why rather than 'not captured this session'.
09_two_devices.png: There is no Android device in this environment and there cannot be one: /dev/kvm is absent, so the x86_64 system image runs under QEMU's own instruction emulation. That was measured rather than assumed — adbd answered after 113 minutes and the framework never came up behind it, so there was no package service to install an APK into. There is no GTK either, so no desktop build can stand in for a second screen, and nothing here was faked from the PWA. docs/PHONES.md records all three routes tried.
16_setup_android.png: The same: the Android first-run screens need an Android device, and this machine has no /dev/kvm. docs/PHONES.md records what was tried and how far each attempt got.
08_state_propagating.png: The far phone is the app's own spine in the host role and has no screen by construction — it is `dart run tool/host_daemon.dart`, not a second copy of the app — and a browser page cannot take that role, because the host binds a listening socket. So the clip shows one screen with the other phone acting on it. docs/PHONES.md says so.
